text:
harper: Planning a rolling maintenance in apac-edge1 on Mon 02:00-05:00 local. Scope: 3 suspect racks showing thermal imbalance + sporadic NIC packet drops. Goal: apply NIC microcode sweep, soft reboot GPUs, validate QoS and KV cache warmup. Reserved pools untouched.

dez: What's the expected shared capacity delta? any parallel cohorts?

harper: If we run serial single-rack cohorts: ~3-6% shared capacity impact. Canary first rack at 02:10 (6 nodes) -> hold 15m -> proceed. No parallel cohorts unless manually approved.

yun: Ops asks: pre-seed prefix/KV caches 40m before start and pause large embedding batches 01:30-06:00. Also prepare hotspot route to apac-west spare pool for tail-sensitive routes.

harper: Agree. Default mitigation: local throttles + async-egress fallback if p95 > +120ms. Cross-region backfill only if error rate >0.4% or p99 > +300ms.

samir: Cost backfill note: pulling 10 GPUs intra-region ~ $500 for 3h; cross-region ~ $1.1k. We'll not auto-backfill unless thresholds exceeded.

ops-bot: Maintenance ticket created: apac-edge1-therm-nic-6601234567. Link: https://console.internal/maint/6601234567 (automated).

harper: Runbook snippet (ops copy):

```bash
# cordon and drain example nodes
kubectl cordon node-ae1-r12{01..06} -n inference
kubectl drain node-ae1-r12{01..06} --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=240 -n inference
# quick net counters
ssh ops@node-ae1-r120 "ethtool -S eth0 | egrep 'rx_errors|tx_errors|rx_dropped'"
# apply nic microcode and reboot
ssh ops@node-ae1-r120 "sudo /usr/bin/apply-nic-fw && sudo reboot"
```

yun: Add a 12-minute manual approval after the canary before expanding. I'll watch model p95/p99 and KV cold-starts. Samir you take cost watch, Dez net.

dez: ACK. I'll prep rollback steps for async-egress flip and BGP route restore.

samir: ACK. I'll make a quick cost dashboard and set auto-alert at $800 burn.

harper: Drafting tenant-facing blurb for non-reserved customers (short window + contact). If no objections we'll schedule the canary. :white_check_mark:
